question:
I'm creating a dbt snapshot from a Snowflake source table. The source table receives a full export regularly, and it contains two important columns: id and inserted_at_utc. Each export inserts a new full dataset.

To snapshot only the latest export, I use this macro:

{% macro snapshot_latest_record(
    source_name,
    table_name,
    timestamp_column='inserted_at_utc',
    exclude_columns='inserted_at_utc'
) %}

    SELECT
        * EXCLUDE ({{ exclude_columns }})
    FROM {{ source(source_name, table_name) }}
    WHERE {{ timestamp_column }} = (
        SELECT MAX({{ timestamp_column }})
        FROM {{ source(source_name, table_name) }}
    )

{% endmacro %}

My snapshot model:

{% snapshot snap_boond__agencies %}

  {{
    config(
      target_schema='SNAPSHOT',
      strategy='check',
      unique_key='ID',
      check_cols='all',
      invalidate_hard_deletes=True,
    )
  }}

  {{ snapshot_latest_record('<source_name>', '<table_name>') }}

{% endsnapshot %}

To verify that the latest export contains no duplicates, I run:

SELECT 
    ID,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        * EXCLUDE (inserted_at_utc)
    FROM <my_table>
    WHERE inserted_at_utc = (
        SELECT MAX(inserted_at_utc)
        FROM <my_table>
    )
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY ID
        ORDER BY inserted_at_utc DESC, ID DESC
    ) = 1
)
GROUP BY ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

This query returns no results, so the source data is not duplicated.

However, dbt still fails with duplicate dbt_scd_id errors:

Failure in test unique_snap_boond__agencies_DBT_SCD_ID
Got 5 results, configured to fail if != 0

And even a full refresh fails:

Database Error in snapshot snap_boond__agencies
100090 (42P18): Duplicate row detected during DML action
Row Values: [redacted]

If the macro returns only one row per ID, why is dbt generating duplicate dbt_scd_id values during the snapshot? What could cause duplicates inside the snapshot table even when the source query itself contains none ?
title: dbt snapshot creates duplicate dbt_scd_id even though source query returns no duplicates
answer:
To verify if data does not contain any duplicates:

SELECT
    * EXCLUDE ({{ exclude_columns }})
FROM {{ source(source_name, table_name) }}
WHERE {{ timestamp_column }} = (
    SELECT MAX({{ timestamp_column }})
    FROM {{ source(source_name, table_name) }}
)
QUALIFY COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY ID) > 1;

The original query using QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() ... = 1 removes duplicates so there is no chance to detect them with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1, if any.

Second ORDER BY inserted_at_utc DESC, ID DESC does not provide reliable way to sort as it is always constant (inserted_at_utc is always the same due to WHERE condition and ID is also the same per partition by):

SELECT 
    ID,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        * EXCLUDE (inserted_at_utc)
    FROM <my_table>
    WHERE inserted_at_utc = (
        SELECT MAX(inserted_at_utc)
        FROM <my_table>
    )
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY ID
        ORDER BY inserted_at_utc DESC, ID DESC
    ) = 1
)
GROUP BY ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
